steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available for building your notification system component.
successCriteria: The import statement should import React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState, which are essential for building React components with state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're importing both React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import React and useState from 'react' using the import statement.

steps.title: Define the Notification interface
steps.instruction: Create a TypeScript interface named 'Notification' with properties: id (string), message (string), type (string), and isRead (boolean).
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and define each property with its type.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Define the Notification interface here
steps.expectedOutcome: The Notification interface is defined with the correct properties and types.
successCriteria: The interface must be named 'Notification' and include id: string, message: string, type: string, and isRead: boolean.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the Notification interface with all required properties and types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that your interface includes all four properties with the correct types: id (string), message (string), type (string), and isRead (boolean).
steps.feedbackWrong: The Notification interface is not correctly defined. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword and include all required properties with their types.

steps.title: Create the NotificationSystem component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component called NotificationSystem that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.hint: Define a component function named NotificationSystem that returns a JSX element like a <div>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A NotificationSystem component function is defined, ready to contain notification system logic and UI.
successCriteria: The component is named NotificationSystem, returns JSX, and uses TypeScript syntax.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created the NotificationSystem component. This is the main container for your notification system.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named NotificationSystem that returns JSX (like a <div>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The NotificationSystem component isn't properly defined. Create a function called NotificationSystem that returns JSX.

steps.title: Initialize notifications state
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, use the useState hook to initialize a state variable called 'notifications' with an empty array of type Notification[].
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. Remember to specify the type as Notification[] and provide an empty array as the initial value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing state with an array type
const [items, setItems] = useState<Item[]>([]);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a notifications state variable initialized as an empty array of Notification objects.
successCriteria: useState hook is called
State variable is named 'notifications'
Type is specified as Notification[]
Initial value is an empty array []
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the notifications state with the correct type and initial value.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using useState with the correct type annotation (Notification[]) and initializing it with an empty array.
steps.feedbackWrong: The state initialization is missing or incorrect. Remember to use useState<Notification[]>([]) to create a notifications state variable.

steps.title: Create addNotification handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, create a function named handleAddNotification that takes two parameters: a string 'message' and a union type 'type' (which can be 'info', 'warning', or 'error'). The function should add a new notification object to the notifications state array.
steps.hint: You'll need to use the setNotifications state setter function. Create a new notification object with a unique id (you can use Date.now() for simplicity), the provided message, and type, then add it to the existing notifications array.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a handleAddNotification function that creates new notification objects and updates the notifications state.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleAddNotification, accept two parameters (message: string, type: 'info' | 'warning' | 'error'), create a new notification object with id, message, and type properties, and update the notifications state by adding the new object to the existing array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleAddNotification function. This function will allow you to add new notifications to the system by updating the state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are some issues. Make sure your function: 1) Has the correct name and parameters, 2) Creates a complete notification object with id, message, and type, and 3) Properly updates the notifications state using setNotifications.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't meet the requirements. Please create a function named handleAddNotification that takes message and type parameters, creates a notification object, and updates the notifications state array.

steps.title: Create markAsRead handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, create a function called handleMarkAsRead that takes a notification id (a number) as a parameter and updates the notifications state to mark that notification as read.
steps.hint: Define a function that accepts an id parameter. Use setNotifications with the previous state to update the specific notification.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a handleMarkAsRead function that can update a notification's read status when called with an id.
successCriteria: The handleMarkAsRead function should be defined inside the component, accept an id parameter of type number, and use setNotifications to update the state.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleMarkAsRead function. This function will allow us to mark specific notifications as read by updating the state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but there are a few issues. Make sure the function accepts an id parameter of type number and properly updates the notifications state using setNotifications.
steps.feedbackWrong: The handleMarkAsRead function is not properly defined. It should be a function that takes an id parameter and updates the notifications state to mark that notification as read.

steps.title: Create clearAllNotifications handler
steps.instruction: Inside the NotificationSystem component, create a function named handleClearAll that sets the notifications state to an empty array.
steps.hint: Use the setNotifications function from useState to update the state with an empty array [].
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleClearAll function is defined that resets the notifications array to empty when called.
successCriteria: Function named handleClearAll is defined
Function calls setNotifications([])
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the handleClearAll function that will clear all notifications.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function is named handleClearAll and calls setNotifications([]).
steps.feedbackWrong: Try again. Create a function named handleClearAll that sets the notifications state to an empty array.

steps.title: Return the main container div
steps.instruction: Update the return statement to wrap the existing content in a div with className 'notification-system'.
steps.hint: Replace the current root div with a div that has the className attribute set to 'notification-system'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a div with className 'notification-system' containing the existing h1 element.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a div element
The div has className='notification-system'
The h1 element is inside this div
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the notification system content in a container div with the appropriate className.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the div has exactly className='notification-system' and contains the h1 element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The main container div with className 'notification-system' is missing or incorrect. Check that you've updated the return statement properly.

steps.title: Add notification header section
steps.instruction: Inside the main container div, add a header section with a title and a clear all button. The button should call the clearAllNotifications handler when clicked.
steps.hint: Create a <div> with a class name like 'notification-header' that contains an <h1> for the title and a <button> with onClick={clearAllNotifications}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of a header section with title and button

Notifications
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will have a header section containing a title and a clear all button that is wired to the clearAllNotifications handler.
successCriteria: Add a header div inside the main container
Include a title element (e.g., h1, h2) in the header
Add a button with onClick={clearAllNotifications}
The button text should indicate clearing all notifications
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the header section with a title and clear button. The button is properly wired to call the clearAllNotifications handler when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some elements, but make sure you have: 1) A header div, 2) A title element inside it, 3) A button with onClick={clearAllNotifications}. Check that all three are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The header section is missing or incomplete. You need to add a header div containing a title and a clear button that calls clearAllNotifications when clicked.

steps.title: Map and display notifications list
steps.instruction: Inside your component's return statement, after the header section, map through the notifications state and render each notification in a div element. Display the notification's message and type inside the div.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the notifications array. For each notification, return a div element with the message and type properties displayed.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will display a list of notifications when the notifications state contains items, showing each notification's message and type in separate div elements.
successCriteria: Use the map method on notifications array
Return a div element for each notification
Display notification.message and notification.type inside the div
Include a key prop using notification.id
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the notifications state and rendered each notification with its message and type. This creates a dynamic list that will update whenever the notifications state changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track with mapping through notifications, but make sure you're displaying both the message and type properties, and including a key prop using notification.id for React's optimization.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on mapping through the notifications array. Remember to use the map method on notifications, return a div for each item, display both message and type, and include a key prop with notification.id.

steps.title: Add mark as read buttons to notifications
steps.instruction: Inside the notification mapping in your component, add a button element to each notification that calls the markAsRead handler with the notification's id when clicked.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element inside the notification mapping. Use onClick={() => markAsRead(notification.id)} to call the handler with the specific notification's id.
steps.expectedOutcome: Each notification in the list will have a 'Mark as Read' button that, when clicked, removes that specific notification from the list.
successCriteria: The code should add a button element inside the notification mapping that calls markAsRead with the notification's id when clicked.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added interactive 'Mark as Read' buttons to each notification. Each button now calls the markAsRead handler with the specific notification's id when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a button element inside the notification mapping that calls markAsRead with the notification's id. Check that you're using onClick={() => markAsRead(notification.id)}.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button for marking notifications as read is missing or not properly implemented. You need to add a button element inside the notification mapping that calls markAsRead with the notification's id when clicked.

steps.title: Add notification creation controls
steps.instruction: Add a form section with input fields and a button to create new notifications. This section should include a text input for the message, a select dropdown for the notification type, and a button that calls the addNotification function with the entered values.
steps.hint: Add this form section before the notifications list. You'll need to create local state for the message input and type selection, then wire the button's onClick to call addNotification with those values.
steps.expectedOutcome: The notification system will have a form section with input fields and a button that allows users to create new notifications by entering a message and selecting a type.
successCriteria: Add state variables for new message input and type selection
Add an input field for the notification message
Add a select dropdown for the notification type with options for 'info', 'warning', and 'error'
Add a button that calls addNotification with the entered values
Place the form section before the notifications list
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the notification creation controls. Users can now create new notifications by entering a message, selecting a type, and clicking the Add Notification button.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some of the notification creation controls, but there are missing elements. Make sure you have: 1) state variables for the message and type, 2) an input field for the message, 3) a select dropdown for the type with all three options, and 4) a button that calls addNotification with the entered values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The notification creation controls are not properly implemented. You need to add a form section with input fields and a button that allows users to create new notifications. This should include state variables for the input values, an input field for the message, a select dropdown for the type, and a button that calls addNotification.
